corpus: PANGAEA Earth and environmental repository metadata. Registry discovery targets and publisher citations were captured November 20, 2026. No dataset files were downloaded.

publisher_frame.retrieval: All result pages sorted by sf-idDataSet ascending. Extract the citation dateTime from each xml-thumb. Dates were compared at day precision.

policy: The common cohort contains works whose publisher citation date falls in the window and whose DOI was registered by its week end. The expanded pooled comparison also admits late registrations through November 18. Unfiltered groups use every descriptive abstract in that cohort. Standalone candidates have an open downloadable dataset, CC BY 4.0 or CC0 and a description. Remove collections, children, explicit versions and supplements before clustering using the existing minimum of three and the production embedding model. Publication date, DOI registration, observation dates and today’s access status are distinct.

publisher_landing_date_checks.additional_sample: Four per week without DOI registration by that week end, ordered by SHA-256 of the lowercase DOI. Some became registered later in the month.

article_and_dataset_comparison.method: Add the 13 free-standing datasets and independent bundles registered by the close of their publication weeks to the same 158 journal articles. Hold weekly input membership fixed in the 28-day comparison. Embed titles and abstracts jointly with allenai/specter2_base, sort identifiers, and apply pipeline.cluster.cluster_items with the same scoring config in both arms. These groups precede editorial screening and ranking.

editorial_check.caucasus: Three glacial-lake inventories supplement one published study. In the 28-day fit they also cluster with a Chilean rock-glacier inventory. The Chilean survey measures another landform in another region.
editorial_check.antarctica: One collection and three records describe a single T19 snow trench. The raw measurements, profiles on a common depth scale and a noise-reduced stack are linked children of the same release.
editorial_check.publication_decision: Keep standalone datasets in source comparison. The registered weekly cohort contained eleven free-standing open datasets. Counting each independent bundle once raises that to thirteen. Neither selection produced an independent three-work dataset group in the pooled month.

limitations: The exact publisher citation day was read from 341 native metadata records and agreed with all 49 individually checked landing pages. Three records in the full 2026 catalogue had no exact citation day. Access, descriptions and related-work links were observed retrospectively on November 20. Publisher pages can appear before DOI registration. Historical first visibility could not be reconstructed for every record. A general reference may describe related research, a shared field campaign or the original source of the data.

publisher_date_comparison.method: Look up all 341 repository identifiers with a publisher citation day from October 22 through November 18. Read the publication date and type, access status, licence and related-work fields from the native metadata XML of every record. Embed the title and descriptive abstract with the production SPECTER2 model. Screen for unrestricted CC BY 4.0 or CC0, descriptive text, a dataset or bundle type and absence of an explicit parent, version or supplement. Retain one record per qualifying bundle. Compare each week and the pooled month with the 158 journal articles. General references, data derived from previous work and shared field campaigns still require editorial review. The records were retrieved retrospectively on November 20.

weekly_editorial_review.decision: exclude as an independent weekly research trend
weekly_editorial_review.reason: Two of the three records describe complementary measurements under drifting ice during Polarstern expedition PS153. Both cite the same expedition report. The third record describes water-column profiles from HEINCKE HE690. The cluster represents two campaigns.

weekly_editorial_review.decision: exclude as an independent weekly research trend
weekly_editorial_review.reason: The two Jamaica Bay records link to each other and cover vehicle and validation measurements from the same September 30, 2025 survey. The third record covers Arctic melt ponds in 2020.

weekly_editorial_review.decision: exclude as an independent weekly research trend
weekly_editorial_review.reason: Three records from the Ocean Acidification International Coordination Centre compilation trace to three original studies. The curators retrieved one dataset from Figshare and two from tables in the cited papers. The studies measured different responses in a diatom, hard clams and chitons. Attach the records to their originating studies.

weekly_editorial_review.decision: exclude as an independent weekly research trend
weekly_editorial_review.reason: Two precipitation-instrument datasets were collected on separate Polarstern cruises in 2024 and 2025. The third record is a multi-cruise instrument series for cloud height and vertical visibility. These products do not establish a common precipitation result across three studies.

pooled_mixed_group_review: One core and the PhaFoS database both report foraminiferal size. The other papers in the group describe seabed sediment grain size and marine benthic traits. The four entries do not share one measured outcome.

The Alaskan dataset measures ground vegetation cover. BorFIT provides aerial laser-scanning training data for individual-tree mapping. The Scottish pinewoods paper reports a long-term ecological resurvey. A shared forest setting does not establish a common measurement or result across the three.
publisher_date_comparison.publication_decision: Keep publisher-date discovery in source comparisons. All four weekly dataset groups were reviewed against publisher descriptions and none qualified as a separate research trend. Preserve dataset-to-study links and check shared campaigns, curated deposits and measured quantities before counting an independent contribution. The eight dataset-only groups in the pooled month are clustering results. The weekly review and two mixed-group checks do not measure precision for all eight pooled groups.
